newsitem.title: ITALY: Milan bourse head urges better communications.
newsitem.headline: Milan bourse head urges better communications.

text.p: The chairman of Italy's stock exchange Francesco Cesarini called for better communications by companies on financial matters on Monday to help encourage the expansion and success of the Milan bourse.
Cesarini was speaking on the opening day of the two-day seventh annual conference of the International Federation of Investor Relations held in Milan.

"If our market wants to grow and become more international, it will have to get rid of one major weakness and of a serious delay vis-a-vis other financial markets when it comes to companies' communications on financial matters," he said.

He said that Italy must continue to narrow the gap in investor relations that exist in Italy compared to other more developed financial marketplaces, to encourage foreign investors into the Italian stock market.

Cesarini added that based on recent analyses there were more than 1,500 companies which could be good flotation candidates, and then gain the advantages of a listing, and promote more interest in the Italian stock exchange.
He said the Milan bourse was working on the setting up of a joint-stock company that will completely take over the organisation, management and development of the stock exchange.
This new style of market is expected to be up and running in six to seven months, Cesarini said.
